book: Thailand's 66-pound ancient rodent Yakamys sirindhornae, known from just two teeth 34 million years old
note: The house keeps this one because it is a giant known from almost nothing: one molar 11.56 millimetres long and a broken front tooth, dug from a coal seam in a Krabi lignite mine in 2004 and only named in November 2026, twenty-two years later. Seven different calculations put Yakamys sirindhornae at about 30 kilograms, 66 pounds, twice the size of any other rodent of its age, living 34 million years ago in the late Eocene. Yak is Thai for giant, mys is Greek for mouse, and the species name honours Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn. The house runs the same way: a whole animal, a whole room, a whole idea can be read from a single tooth left in the dark, and the naming can wait decades while the thing itself waits to be seen.
